resources.string: Speed of sound in tube air (v)

The lowest standing-wave mode fits one quarter-wavelength in a tube with one open end and one closed end. Fundamental frequency (Hz) = v / (4L), with v in m/s and L converted from cm to m. A longer tube lowers the fundamental at fixed speed; faster sound raises it at fixed length.

These made-up values describe a straight, rigid classroom tube, not a real ear or personal measurement. The real ear canal is not a rigid pipe: it curves, varies in width, and ends at a vibrating eardrum rather than an ideal sealed end. This analogy does not predict individual hearing.
